A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PixNet for dense spatial gene-expression prediction. All pages, equations, tables, figures and references support comparison; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, cross-resolution generalization experiments, encoder and spot-size ablations, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on four datasets, cross-resolution generalization, ablations and qualitative predictions in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The decoder changes from deconvolution, learnably scaled additive skip fusion and DFFN blocks to depth-to-space upsampling in deep stages, bilinear upsampling in shallow stages and residual linear attention fusion. The output head also changes to a 1x1 convolution. The encoder, spot aggregation and sparse MSE-plus-PCC objective remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds Her2ST, described as 36 slides and approximately 13K spots at 100 µm from HER2-positive breast tumors. This adds a breast-tumor cohort while retaining the existing breast/brain coverage, prediction task and tested spatial scales.

E2.justification: v2 adds HGGEP, Junayed et al. (2024), BG-TRIPLEX, ScstGCN and MERGE to comparisons on the retained datasets and to cross-resolution generalization. All seven earlier comparators remain, substantially expanding the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: Implementation Details changes PixNet training from 500 to 200 epochs, a substantial reported budget reduction. The stated optimizer, learning rate, weight decay, gene selection, normalization, metrics and cross-fold protocol references remain unchanged. This revision does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds a GNAS prediction example at 100 µm, extending the qualitative case evidence. The encoder choices, spot-size combinations and cross-resolution generalization questions are retained; no ablation isolating the new decoder components is added.

E5.justification: Both versions use ± reporting in benchmark and spot-size tables and explicitly omit standard deviations from the generalization table. Neither adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures; additional rows and revised values do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds Her2ST and new-comparator results and revises existing entries. PixNet's brain-dataset PCC@M changes from 0.202 to 0.236, and its 2 µm transfer PCC@M from 0.160 to 0.164. HistoGene's STNet scores and spot-size/encoder ablation values also change. PixNet's revised scores accompany architecture and training-budget changes, so they are not controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The decoder's mathematical definitions are revised: v1 Eqs. 3–4 give way to upsampling, feature-refinement, attention and fusion definitions in v2 Eqs. 3–8. The encoder, circular aggregation domain and loss formulation remain mathematically unchanged; no theorem, proof or formal generalization guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the state-of-the-art performance claim from three datasets to four. The central contributions—dense expression prediction, sparse supervision and prediction across spatial scales—retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism arguments about preserving spatial information through staged upsampling and feature refinement. Its new Limitation section explicitly identifies dependence on experimentally measured supervision and proposes unsupervised or self-supervised learning as future work.

D1.justification: v2 provides implementation specifics for the revised decoder, including convolution sizes, normalization, activation and upsampling details, and revises the epoch setting. Most other training details remain. The direct Visium dataset URL present in v1 is removed, while the named source remains; both versions only promise future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial related-work section covering spatial-expression predictors and dense medical-image prediction. It acknowledges iSTar's pixel-wise predictions and distinguishes PixNet from super-resolution approaches. New decoder positioning cites Wazir and Kim, replacing the earlier DFFN-related reference.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental discussion are broadly rewritten, and the decoder explanation is reorganized and expanded. An explicit contribution list and separate Related work and Limitation sections substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 1–2 are substantially redrawn, Figure 3 gains a case, and the benchmark table is reorganized into two tables with expanded comparisons. Figure 4 is reformatted and its PCC axis range changes.

improvement.justification: The added Her2ST evaluation and broader comparator set strengthen an already multi-dataset empirical study. The new discussion of pixel-wise prior work and dependence on measured supervision improves assessment of novelty and applicability. These are useful gains, but the redesigned decoder lacks component ablations, and the simultaneous training-budget change prevents isolating its benefit from the revised scores.
